situation (example wording): "Murders through April for each year from 2017 through 2025 in Baltimore city", "Houston murders in the first 6 months of each year", "homicides in the first half of 2023"
what the app does today: Declined: "I didn't understand through April" (or the first six months).
proposed behavior: A question that names a month to count through ("through April", "January through June") or the first N months ("first 6 months", "first half"), with one year or several years named, or "each year" and no range (every year in the data, said), counts January through that month of each year. A question with no year and no "each year" keeps its decline (it is not read as every year), and with no place named it is the United States (P180, which supersedes the ask). One year is its own figure; several years are one table Year | figure, each year the sum of its months from the engine's own monthly answer, so its source and limits apply. A year with any month not known is blank, never a partial sum, and the answer says which month. The title names the months ("Baltimore, Maryland: murders January through April, 2017 to 2025.") and one line says each year counts the same months. The months are never dropped for the whole year: a question the app cannot answer this way (several places, a day of the month) is declined. Year-to-date comparisons ("YTD 2026 compared to 2025") are not part of this row.
exact default or choices offered: Table Year | figure for January through the named month of each year; the months named in the title.
why: Jeff 2026-11-16 (Q1, through the coordinator): "table Year | Murders, each year counting the named months, title names the months; same shape for first 6 months of each year."
